title: Cable rib lap throw
subtitle: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw in alternating rib and cable columns, aran weight.
excerpt: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw in aran weight on 5 mm needles. The pattern repeats: two knit stitches, six-stitch cable, two purl stitches, across the full width. The regular cable column rhythm gives the throw a structured, classic look. About 700 g of aran.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 10th series (1894), §Cable and Rib Throws, documents an all-over cable-rib structure for large throws as a standard Victorian sofa cover pattern. Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Cable Stitches, describes the six-stitch cable-front crossing used here.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts × 24 rows = 10 × 10 cm in cable-rib pattern on 5 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stitch pattern where a cable column (typically 6 stitches) is alternated with a purl-column separator (typically 2 stitches) in a regular repeat across the full width. The purl columns create the visual rib between cables. On right-side rows, the cable columns are knitted (or cabled) and the purl columns are purled. On wrong-side rows, everything is reversed.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 5 mm needles. The pattern is a regular
cable-rib repeat
: six-stitch cables with two-purl separators. Finished size: 100 cm wide by 120 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. The cable-rib repeat is self-finishing: the purl columns at each side edge form the side borders and the repeated cables naturally pull the fabric into a flat, non-curling piece. Aran weight was chosen for drape and speed; the cables read clearly at the larger stitch size. Budget about 700 g (about 1,240 m / 1,355 yards) of aran. A cable needle is required. Buy in matched dye lots.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 700 g (about 1,240 m / 1,355 yards) of aran-weight yarn. Smooth aran shows cable definition best.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, 120 cm or longer

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: Several (to mark cable positions within the repeat)

content.text: Gauge

18 stitches and 24 rows to 10 cm in cable-rib pattern on 5 mm needles, blocked. Cable-rib draws in significantly before blocking; the unblocked width will be 8 to 10 cm narrower than the blocked width. Measure gauge after a wash and flat dry, not off the needle.
The repeat is 8 stitches (6 cable + 2 purl). With 180 stitches, there are 22 complete repeats and 4 edge stitches. At 18 stitches per 10 cm, 180 stitches produces 100 cm after blocking.
Stitches used

items.name: C6F
items.qty: sl3 to cable needle hold front, k3, k3 from cable needle

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 180 stitches (a multiple of 8, plus 4 edge stitches). Long-tail tail: (5 × 180) / 10 + 15 = 90 + 15 = 105 cm. Measure 120 cm.
Body
RS rows (non-cable): p2, *k6, p2; repeat from * to end.
RS cable rows (every 8 rows, starting at row 5): p2, *C6F, p2; repeat from * to end.
WS rows: k2, *p6, k2; repeat from * to end.
Continue until the throw measures 120 cm. When you set this aside, note the row in the 8-row cable cycle.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 144 (about 60 cm): count across. You should have 180 stitches. Cables do not change stitch count. At row 286 (about 119 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults
Cables irregular in size: different cable crossings have different numbers of stitches (sometimes 4, sometimes 6). Confirm 3 stitches are on the cable needle before each C6F.

Purl columns tighter than the cable columns: purl tension is naturally looser for some knitters, but tighter for others when purling within a cable-dense row. Check that the purl columns in the WS row are worked at the same tension as the RS.
Cast-off
Cast off in pattern (k the knits, p the purls) with needles one size larger to keep the edge elastic. Cable-rib blankets need an elastic cast-off edge.
Finishing
Weave in ends. Block firmly with steam or by wetting to open the cables and relax the rib. The blocked throw will be significantly wider and more even than the unblocked piece.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash aran. Lay flat to dry. Re-block if the cables close up after washing.
What to try next

From a regular cable-rib, try a mixed-cable throw next. The cable width varies across the width. A central twelve-stitch rope sits between eight-stitch honeycomb cables. Four-stitch rope cables run at the edges, separated by two-stitch purl ribs.
